lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Supervised application: secure storage of sensitive documents

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic secure storage of sensitive documents task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: With a trusted adult, the learner discusses and records, at a category level only, where important documents could be kept securely in their household (for example, a locked drawer, a folder a guardian keeps, or a password-protected note that itself contains no real passwords) and confirms the plan is one the household could actually use.
safetyNotes: The conversation covers where documents would be kept, never their actual contents, numbers, or any password or PIN.
No password, PIN, or account credential is ever written down as part of this task, even as an example.
If a household genuinely has no secure storage option right now, naming that gap honestly is an acceptable outcome — the task is the conversation and the honest plan, not a guaranteed 'yes.'

simulationAlternative.description: If no adult is available for this conversation today, the learner instead designs a secure-storage plan for a fictional household using the same categories and criteria, and explains what they would ask a real adult about when one is available.

materials: learner-local: paper or a notes document

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l04-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Was there a category that turned out to be more complicated to discuss than you expected? What made it complicated?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g12-u01-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Conversation completeness: The summary reflects a conversation that covered both physical and digital storage categories. | Privacy discipline: No credential of any kind appears; only storage categories and locations are described. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner identify one document category not on the provided checklist that applies to their situation, and add it to the plan with the adult's input.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic secure storage of sensitive documents task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

localMaterials.label: paper or a notes document
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: secure storage of sensitive documents worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: With a trusted adult, the learner discusses and records, at a category level only, where important documents could be kept securely in their household (for example, a locked drawer, a folder a guardian keeps, or a password-protected note that itself contains no real passwords) and confirms the plan is one the household could actually use.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact secure storage of sensitive documents decision or action.
Model move 2: Before the conversation, list what you think 'secure' means for a physical document versus a digital one.
Model move 3: With your adult, talk through where important documents could realistically be kept in your household and record the plan by category.

Model check: Conversation completeness: The summary reflects a conversation that covered both physical and digital storage categories. | Privacy discipline: No credential of any kind appears; only storage categories and locations are described.

resources.title: secure storage of sensitive documents action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for secure storage of sensitive documents.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: secure storage of sensitive documents coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: With a trusted adult, the learner discusses and records, at a category level only, where important documents could be kept securely in their household (for example, a locked drawer, a folder a guardian keeps, or a password-protected note that itself contains no real passwords) and confirms the plan is one the household could actually use.
Coach direction: Before the conversation, list what you think 'secure' means for a physical document versus a digital one.
Learner prompt: In your own words, what makes storage 'secure' for a paper document, and what makes storage 'secure' for a digital one? They don't have to be the same answer.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: secure storage of sensitive documents complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult, talk through where important documents could realistically be kept in your household and record the plan by category.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I talked with an adult about where physical documents could be kept securely.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I talked with an adult about where digital records or accounts could be kept securely, without writing down any actual password.
Response 3 (t2-p3): My adult confirmed the plan is realistic for our household, or we honestly named a gap instead.

Equal-access rule: If no adult is available for this conversation today, the learner instead designs a secure-storage plan for a fictional household using the same categories and criteria, and explains what they would ask a real adult about when one is available.

resources.title: secure storage of sensitive documents minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Was there a category that turned out to be more complicated to discuss than you expected? What made it complicated?

Success checks: Conversation completeness: The summary reflects a conversation that covered both physical and digital storage categories. | Privacy discipline: No credential of any kind appears; only storage categories and locations are described.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: secure storage of sensitive documents supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g12-u01-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional secure storage of sensitive documents condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Conversation completeness: The summary reflects a conversation that covered both physical and digital storage categories. | Privacy discipline: No credential of any kind appears; only storage categories and locations are described..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u01-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
